title: Set and use OKRs
summary: Objectives and key results, or OKRs, pair an inspiring goal with a few measurable results. Used well, they focus a team on outcomes rather than a list of tasks.

beginner: Write one to three objectives: short statements of what you want to achieve.
For each, write three to five key results that measure progress. They should be outcomes, not tasks.
Check each key result has a baseline and a target.
Review progress every two to four weeks.
Score them honestly at the end and learn from the misses.
intermediate: Draft objectives linked to company goals.
Review progress regularly and adjust work.
experienced: Align OKRs across teams without creating a rigid hierarchy.
Use OKRs to drive conversations about trade-offs.
Coach teams to write outcomes, not output.

toolExamples.confluence: Use an OKR template page and update it each review.
toolExamples.notion: Keep OKRs in a database linked to roadmap items.
toolExamples.jira: Link epics to the key result they move.

pitfalls: Setting them and not looking again until the end
